$comment: Copy to .claude/config/lint-gate.json in your project. Both keys are optional, and there
are no defaults: a command is only run if the project asked for it by name.
format  runs after every Edit/Write, on that one file, from the file's checkout. Use
{file} to place the path, otherwise it is appended. The path is shell-quoted.
checks  run in list order on Stop and TeammateIdle, never per edit, and every failure
is reported together.
Formatting is per-edit because it is a syntactic transform that is valid on any file
that parses. Checks are not: an import added in one edit and used in the next reads as
an unused import in between. Reporting that would train the agent to undo correct work.
Each check:
name        required, unique
scope       required: how the result is attributed to the session
files    gets the edited files through {files}; for linters
program  runs whole, once per build unit; for typecheckers. Never {files}:
tsc handed paths ignores tsconfig.json and appears to pass
unit     a verdict with no file locations; for tests, builds, cdk synth
command     run at Stop; or
watch       unit only: a watcher started on the first matching edit, read at Stop
when        glob or list of globs, relative to the checkout root. The check is owed
only if an edited path matches. Default: any edit. Cover what the unit
depends on, not only its own folder.
cwd         where the command runs, relative to the checkout root
report      program only. "all" (default): exit code decides. "edited": only errors
located in files the session edited block. For units with a backlog.
parse       with report "edited": tsc, mypy, mypy-json, pyright-json,
svelte-check-machine. Call the tool directly (npx tsc --pretty false),
not through npm run: any line the parser cannot read fails the check.
timeoutSec  default 180; a check that runs longer fails
A session that edited nothing owes no check. Edits are recorded from Write, Edit,
MultiEdit and NotebookEdit, and from what Claude Code reports a Bash command changed.
Paths outside the project, or that no longer exist, are dropped; an edit inside a git
worktree is checked from that worktree.
watch needs {status}: the gate owns that path and reads JSON from it, expecting a
boolean `success` (numFailedTests and numTotalTests are used for the message). A report
that is missing, older than the last matching edit, or unreadable blocks the turn.
Freshness is the file's mtime, not any timestamp inside it: vitest's JSON reporter
leaves startTime at the first run for the life of the watch process.
Node's built-in test runner has no reporter that writes a verdict, so lint-gate ships one:
"watch": "LINT_GATE_STATUS={status} node --test --watch --test-reporter=${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/reporters/node-test-json.mjs"
The path comes through the environment rather than --test-reporter-destination: under
--watch the reporter's event stream never ends, so one that emits after its loop never emits.
